{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:

let
  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;

  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    # installs the CLI as `orca-ide`, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    # meta.mainProgram use below. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin
    # name, so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    #
    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    # is a flag on the command line.
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bin/orca symlink from buildCommand
    # is replaced with a wrapper that prepends the flag and passes "$@"
    # through. buildFHSEnv's builder has no makeWrapper on PATH, so its setup
    # hook is sourced by hand; and the wrapper must not target its own path
    # (renaming to orca-ide and wrapping orca-ide in place makes it exec
    # itself), so the bwrap launcher moves aside to .orca-ide-unwrapped.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      source ${pkgs.makeWrapper}/nix-support/setup-hook
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      makeShellWrapper $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped $out/bin/orca-ide \
        --add-flags '--ozone-platform=wayland'
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below;
  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. Ctrl then
  # goes back to the terminal: Ctrl+C is SIGINT again, not copy.
  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
  # Chords Hyprland binds are skipped and those actions keep their Linux Ctrl
  # default -- the compositor would eat them, leaving a dead key. That costs
  # Super+F (find), Super+P (go to file), Super+N and Super+B, which are
  # Hyprland's emacs-style focus moves; the build log lists every one.
  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
    lib.concatMap
      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (lib.hasPrefix "bind") (builtins.attrNames s));
  macKeybindings = pkgs.runCommand "orca-mac-keybindings" {
    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper ];
  } ''
    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \
      > $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
    makeWrapper ${mergeKeybindings} $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \
      --set OWNED $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
  '';
  # ~/.orca/keybindings.json is Orca's read-write state: its settings UI saves
  # into the same platforms.linux section, by atomic rename, so a home.file
  # symlink would be replaced on the first edit. So the generated keys are
  # merged over whatever Orca last wrote -- they win, every other action's UI

{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:

let
  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;

  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    # installs the CLI as `orca-ide`, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    # meta.mainProgram use below. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin
    # name, so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    #
    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    # is a flag on the command line.
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bin/orca symlink from buildCommand
    # is replaced with a wrapper that prepends the flag and passes "$@"
    # through. buildFHSEnv's builder has no makeWrapper on PATH, so its setup
    # hook is sourced by hand; and the wrapper must not target its own path
    # (renaming to orca-ide and wrapping orca-ide in place makes it exec
    # itself), so the bwrap launcher moves aside to .orca-ide-unwrapped.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      source ${pkgs.makeWrapper}/nix-support/setup-hook
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      makeShellWrapper $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped $out/bin/orca-ide \
        --add-flags '--ozone-platform=wayland'
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';

  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. Ctrl then
  # goes back to the terminal: Ctrl+C is SIGINT again, not copy.
  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
  # Chords Hyprland binds are skipped and those actions keep their Linux Ctrl
  # default -- the compositor would eat them, leaving a dead key. That costs
  # Super+F (find), Super+P (go to file), Super+N and Super+B, which are
  # Hyprland's emacs-style focus moves; the build log lists every one.
  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
    lib.concatMap
      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (lib.hasPrefix "bind") (builtins.attrNames s));

    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper ];
  } ''
    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \
      > $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
    # The merge runs Orca's conflict check on the merged file at activation,
    # so the keybinding module (and its one sibling import) ships alongside.
    mkdir -p $out/lib/shared
    cp -r app/out/shared/keybindings.js app/out/shared/keybindings \
      app/out/shared/tui-agent-display-names.js $out/lib/shared/
    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \
      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
  '';
  # ~/.orca/keybindings.json is Orca's read-write state: its settings UI saves
  # into the same platforms.linux section, by atomic rename, so a home.file
  # symlink would be replaced on the first edit. So the generated keys are
  # merged into whatever Orca last wrote, owning only what the last merge
  # wrote (a sidecar records it), and a UI edit outranks them -- the rules
  # are at the top of nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js.
  # tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh.
in
{
  home.packages =
    lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop) [
    # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
    # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
    # same reason parsec gets it.
      (config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca)
    ];

  home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop)
    (lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" ] ''
      $DRY_RUN_CMD ${macKeybindings}/bin/orca-mac-keybindings
    '');
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for orca.nix's Mac-style keybindings: Orca's own macOS defaults, with
# Cmd on Super, merged into ~/.orca/keybindings.json at activation.
#
# Two contracts, both silent when broken:
#
#   * **No chord Hyprland owns.** The compositor eats a bound chord before the
#     window sees it, so a Super+F override is not "find", it is a dead key that
#     also hides Orca's working Ctrl+F default. The generator drops those and
#     leaves the action on its Linux default; cases 2-3 pin that against the
#     live Hyprland bind list, not a copy of it.
#
#   * **The merge owns only its keys.** Orca's settings UI writes into the same
#     platforms.linux section, so replacing the section would wipe every
#     shortcut set in the UI at each switch. Cases 5-6.
#
# The merge runs on a throwaway HOME, never the real ~/.orca.
#
#   tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh                   evaluate + build, then test
#   tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh <merge-package>   test a given build
set -u
set -o pipefail

fails=0; n=0
pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(hostname).config"

PKG="${1:-}"
if [ -z "$PKG" ]; then
  # The activation entry's string context names the merge package's drv.
  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings.data" \
    --apply 'd: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext d))' 2>/dev/null) \
    || { echo "no home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings on this host" >&2; exit 1; }
  PKG=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build $drv" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
MERGE="$PKG/bin/orca-mac-keybindings"
OWNED="$PKG/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
[ -x "$MERGE" ] && [ -f "$OWNED" ] || { echo "$PKG lacks bin/ or share/" >&2; exit 1; }

T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
jqo() { jq -c "$1" "$OWNED"; }

# 1. The Mac table, on Super: clipboard and tabs are the reason this exists.
for c in 'terminal.copySelection:["Cmd+C"]' 'terminal.paste:["Cmd+V"]' \
         'tab.close:["Cmd+W"]' 'tab.newTerminal:["Cmd+T"]'; do
  id=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
  got=$(jqo ".[\"$id\"]")
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$id = $want" || fail "$id" "got $got, want $want"
done
got=$(jqo '[.[][] | select(test("(^|\\+)Mod\\+"))]')
[ "$got" = "[]" ] && pass "no Mod (= Ctrl on Linux) left" || fail "Mod" "still bound: $got"

# 2. Nothing the generator emits is a Hyprland chord.
nix eval --json "$HM.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings" --apply \
  's: builtins.concatMap (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (k: builtins.substring 0 4 k == "bind") (builtins.attrNames s))' \
  2>/dev/null > "$T/hypr.json" || { echo "could not evaluate Hyprland binds" >&2; exit 1; }
# Hyprland "SUPER + SHIFT + W" -> Orca "Cmd+Shift+W"; letters upper-cased, the
# keys Orca spells differently renamed. Mouse and switch binds never match.
jq -r '.[] | split(" + ") | map(
    {SUPER:"Cmd",CTRL:"Ctrl",ALT:"Alt",SHIFT:"Shift",
     return:"Enter",left:"ArrowLeft",right:"ArrowRight",up:"ArrowUp",down:"ArrowDown",
     space:"Space",semicolon:"Semicolon"}[.] // (if length == 1 then ascii_upcase else . end))
  | join("+")' "$T/hypr.json" | sort -u > "$T/hypr.txt"
grep -qx 'Cmd+F' "$T/hypr.txt" || { echo "Hyprland bind list lacks Super+F; harness is broken" >&2; exit 1; }
jq -r '.[][]' "$OWNED" | sort -u > "$T/owned.txt"
clash=$(comm -12 "$T/hypr.txt" "$T/owned.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "$clash" ] && pass "no override is a Hyprland chord" || fail "hyprland" "both bind: $clash"

# 3. A chord Hyprland owns leaves its action on Orca's Linux default, not unbound.
got=$(jqo 'has("editor.find"), has("worktree.quickOpen")' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ "$got" = "false false " ] && pass "Super+F/Super+P actions keep their Linux defaults" \
  || fail "fallback" "editor.find/worktree.quickOpen overridden: $got"

# 4. Fresh box: the file is created in the shape Orca writes.
H="$T/fresh"; mkdir -p "$H"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c --slurpfile o "$OWNED" '[.version, (.platforms.linux == $o[0]), .keybindings, .platforms.darwin]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" 2>/dev/null)
[ "$got" = '[1,true,{},{}]' ] && pass "fresh HOME gets a version-1 file" || fail "fresh" "got $got"

# 5. Owned keys win; UI edits to other actions, common and darwin survive.
H="$T/edited"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{"tab.rename":["Alt+R"]},
 "platforms":{"darwin":{"tab.close":["Cmd+Q"]},"linux":{"tab.close":["Ctrl+Q"],"editor.find":["Alt+F"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["tab.close"], .platforms.linux["editor.find"], .keybindings, .platforms.darwin]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[["Cmd+W"],["Alt+F"],{"tab.rename":["Alt+R"]},{"tab.close":["Cmd+Q"]}]' ] \
  && pass "merge keeps UI edits outside its keys" || fail "merge" "got $got"

# 6. A file Orca cannot parse is left alone; activation does not fail on it.
H="$T/broken"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"; printf '{not json' > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json"
if HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(cat "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")" = '{not json' ] \
   && [ ! -e "$H/.orca/keybindings.json.new" ]; then
  pass "unparseable file untouched, exit 0"
else
  fail "broken" "file changed, .new left behind, or non-zero exit"
fi

# 7. A key an earlier generation wrote, and this one no longer emits (Hyprland
#    took the chord, say), is removed -- unless the UI has changed it since.
#    A generated key the UI changed after it was written stays the UI's.
H="$T/stale"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{},
 "platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Alt+P"],"tab.close":["Ctrl+Q"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
echo '{"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Cmd+P"],"tab.close":["Cmd+W"]}}' \
  > "$H/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["editor.find"], .platforms.linux["worktree.quickOpen"], .platforms.linux["tab.close"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[null,["Alt+P"],["Ctrl+Q"]]' ] && pass "stale generated key dropped, UI-changed ones kept" \
  || fail "stale" "got $got"

# 8. A UI shortcut on a generated chord: Orca would drop *both* actions at load.
#    The UI's choice stands; the generated action falls back to its default.
H="$T/clash"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{},"platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{"tab.newBrowser":["Cmd+T"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
err=$(HOME=$H "$MERGE" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["tab.newBrowser"], .platforms.linux["tab.newTerminal"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
if [ "$got" = '[["Cmd+T"],null]' ] && [[ $err == *tab.newTerminal* ]]; then
  pass "UI chord wins a clash, and the dropped key is named"
else
  fail "clash" "got $got, stderr '$err'"
fi

# 9. An empty file is not JSON either: left alone, not "merged" into nothing.
H="$T/empty"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"; : > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json"
if HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ ! -s "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" ]; then
  pass "empty file untouched, exit 0"
else
  fail "empty" "file rewritten or non-zero exit"
fi

printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for orca.nix's Mac-style keybindings: Orca's own macOS defaults, with
# Cmd on Super, merged into ~/.orca/keybindings.json at activation.
#
# Two contracts, both silent when broken:
#
#   * **No chord Hyprland owns.** The compositor eats a bound chord before the
#     window sees it, so a Super+F override is not "find", it is a dead key that
#     also hides Orca's working Ctrl+F default. The generator drops those and
#     leaves the action on its Linux default; cases 2-3 pin that against the
#     live Hyprland bind list, not a copy of it.
#
#   * **The merge owns only its keys.** Orca's settings UI writes into the same
#     platforms.linux section, so replacing the section would wipe every
#     shortcut set in the UI at each switch. Cases 5-6.
#
# The merge runs on a throwaway HOME, never the real ~/.orca.
#
#   tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh                   evaluate + build, then test
#   tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh <merge-package>   test a given build
set -u
set -o pipefail

fails=0; n=0
pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }

FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(hostname).config"

PKG="${1:-}"
if [ -z "$PKG" ]; then
  # The activation entry's string context names the merge package's drv.
  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings.data" \
    --apply 'd: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext d))' 2>/dev/null) \
    || { echo "no home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings on this host" >&2; exit 1; }
  PKG=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build $drv" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
MERGE="$PKG/bin/orca-mac-keybindings"
OWNED="$PKG/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
[ -x "$MERGE" ] && [ -f "$OWNED" ] || { echo "$PKG lacks bin/ or share/" >&2; exit 1; }

T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
jqo() { jq -c "$1" "$OWNED"; }

# 1. The Mac table, on Super: clipboard and tabs are the reason this exists.
for c in 'terminal.copySelection:["Cmd+C"]' 'terminal.paste:["Cmd+V"]' \
         'tab.close:["Cmd+W"]' 'tab.newTerminal:["Cmd+T"]'; do
  id=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
  got=$(jqo ".[\"$id\"]")
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$id = $want" || fail "$id" "got $got, want $want"
done
got=$(jqo '[.[][] | select(test("(^|\\+)Mod\\+"))]')
[ "$got" = "[]" ] && pass "no Mod (= Ctrl on Linux) left" || fail "Mod" "still bound: $got"

# 2. Nothing the generator emits is a Hyprland chord.
nix eval --json "$HM.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings" --apply \
  's: builtins.concatMap (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (k: builtins.substring 0 4 k == "bind") (builtins.attrNames s))' \
  2>/dev/null > "$T/hypr.json" || { echo "could not evaluate Hyprland binds" >&2; exit 1; }
# Hyprland "SUPER + SHIFT + W" -> Orca "Cmd+Shift+W"; letters upper-cased, the
# keys Orca spells differently renamed. Mouse and switch binds never match.
jq -r '.[] | split(" + ") | map(
    {SUPER:"Cmd",CTRL:"Ctrl",ALT:"Alt",SHIFT:"Shift",
     return:"Enter",left:"ArrowLeft",right:"ArrowRight",up:"ArrowUp",down:"ArrowDown",
     space:"Space",semicolon:"Semicolon"}[.] // (if length == 1 then ascii_upcase else . end))
  | join("+")' "$T/hypr.json" | sort -u > "$T/hypr.txt"
grep -qx 'Cmd+F' "$T/hypr.txt" || { echo "Hyprland bind list lacks Super+F; harness is broken" >&2; exit 1; }
jq -r '.[][]' "$OWNED" | sort -u > "$T/owned.txt"
clash=$(comm -12 "$T/hypr.txt" "$T/owned.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "$clash" ] && pass "no override is a Hyprland chord" || fail "hyprland" "both bind: $clash"

# 3. A chord Hyprland owns leaves its action on Orca's Linux default, not unbound.
got=$(jqo 'has("editor.find"), has("worktree.quickOpen")' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ "$got" = "false false " ] && pass "Super+F/Super+P actions keep their Linux defaults" \
  || fail "fallback" "editor.find/worktree.quickOpen overridden: $got"

# 4. Fresh box: the file is created in the shape Orca writes.
H="$T/fresh"; mkdir -p "$H"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c --slurpfile o "$OWNED" '[.version, (.platforms.linux == $o[0]), .keybindings, .platforms.darwin]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" 2>/dev/null)
[ "$got" = '[1,true,{},{}]' ] && pass "fresh HOME gets a version-1 file" || fail "fresh" "got $got"
cp "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" "$T/first.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
cmp -s "$T/first.json" "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" && pass "second switch changes nothing" \
  || fail "idempotent" "re-running the merge rewrote the file"

# 5. Owned keys win; UI edits to other actions, common and darwin survive.
H="$T/edited"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{"tab.rename":["Alt+R"]},
 "platforms":{"darwin":{"tab.close":["Cmd+Q"]},"linux":{"tab.close":["Ctrl+Q"],"editor.find":["Alt+F"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["tab.close"], .platforms.linux["editor.find"], .keybindings, .platforms.darwin]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[["Cmd+W"],["Alt+F"],{"tab.rename":["Alt+R"]},{"tab.close":["Cmd+Q"]}]' ] \
  && pass "merge keeps UI edits outside its keys" || fail "merge" "got $got"

# 6. A file Orca cannot parse is left alone; activation does not fail on it.
H="$T/broken"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"; printf '{not json' > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json"
if HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(cat "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")" = '{not json' ] \
   && [ ! -e "$H/.orca/keybindings.json.new" ]; then
  pass "unparseable file untouched, exit 0"
else
  fail "broken" "file changed, .new left behind, or non-zero exit"
fi

# 7. A key an earlier generation wrote, and this one no longer emits (Hyprland
#    took the chord, say), is removed -- unless the UI has changed it since.
#    A generated key the UI changed after it was written stays the UI's.
H="$T/stale"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{},
 "platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Alt+P"],"tab.close":["Ctrl+Q"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
echo '{"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Cmd+P"],"tab.close":["Cmd+W"]}}' \
  > "$H/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1

# 6. A file Orca cannot parse is left alone; activation does not fail on it.
H="$T/broken"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"; printf '{not json' > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json"
if HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(cat "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")" = '{not json' ] \
   && [ -z "$(ls "$H/.orca" | grep -v "^keybindings.json$")" ]; then
  pass "unparseable file untouched, exit 0"
else
  fail "broken" "file changed, .new left behind, or non-zero exit"
fi
# 7. A key an earlier generation wrote, and this one no longer emits (Hyprland
#    took the chord, say), is removed -- unless the UI has changed it since.
#    A generated key the UI changed after it was written stays the UI's.
H="$T/stale"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{},
 "platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Alt+P"],"tab.close":["Ctrl+Q"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
echo '{"linux":{"editor.find":["Cmd+F"],"worktree.quickOpen":["Cmd+P"],"tab.close":["Cmd+W"]}}' \
  > "$H/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["editor.find"], .platforms.linux["worktree.quickOpen"], .platforms.linux["tab.close"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[null,["Alt+P"],["Ctrl+Q"]]' ] && pass "stale generated key dropped, UI-changed ones kept" \
  || fail "stale" "got $got"

#     leaves the action on its Linux default; cases 2-3 pin that against the

OWNED="$PKG/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"

  fail "broken" "file changed, .new left behind, or non-zero exit"

#    took the chord, say), is removed -- unless the UI has changed it since.

  > "$H/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["editor.find"], .platforms.linux["worktree.quickOpen"], .platforms.linux["tab.close"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[null,["Alt+P"],["Ctrl+Q"]]' ] && pass "stale generated key dropped, UI-changed ones kept" \
  || fail "stale" "got $got"

#    The UI's choice stands; the generated action falls back to its default.
H="$T/clash"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
cat > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json" <<'EOF'
{"version":1,"keybindings":{},"platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{"tab.newBrowser":["Cmd+T"]},"win32":{}}}
EOF
err=$(HOME=$H "$MERGE" 2>&1 >/dev/null)
got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["tab.newBrowser"], .platforms.linux["tab.newTerminal"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")

EOF

got=$(jq -c '[.platforms.linux["tab.newBrowser"], .platforms.linux["tab.newTerminal"]]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '[["Cmd+T"],["Alt+N"]]' ] && pass "withdrawn key restores the UI's value, across switches" \
  || fail "clash-restore" "got $got"

  pass "empty file untouched, exit 0"
else
  fail "empty" "file rewritten or non-zero exit"
fi

{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:

let
  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;

  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # The AppImage ships bin/orca and an orca-ide.desktop; upstream's .deb
    # installs the CLI as `orca-ide`, and that is what the desktop Exec and
    # meta.mainProgram use below. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin
    # name, so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    #
    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    # is a flag on the command line.
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bin/orca symlink from buildCommand
    # is replaced with a wrapper that prepends the flag and passes "$@"
    # through. buildFHSEnv's builder has no makeWrapper on PATH, so its setup
    # hook is sourced by hand; and the wrapper must not target its own path
    # (renaming to orca-ide and wrapping orca-ide in place makes it exec
    # itself), so the bwrap launcher moves aside to .orca-ide-unwrapped.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      source ${pkgs.makeWrapper}/nix-support/setup-hook
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      makeShellWrapper $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped $out/bin/orca-ide \
        --add-flags '--ozone-platform=wayland'
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below;
  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. Ctrl then
  # goes back to the terminal: Ctrl+C is SIGINT again, not copy. Except where
  # the Mac table itself says Ctrl: Ctrl+1..9 selects a tab (Linux: Alt+1..9),
  # Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+PageUp/Down cycle them, as on a Mac.
  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
  # Chords Hyprland binds are skipped and those actions keep their Linux Ctrl
  # default -- the compositor would eat them, leaving a dead key. That costs
  # Super+F (find), Super+P (go to file), Super+N and Super+B, which are
  # Hyprland's emacs-style focus moves; the build log lists every one.
  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
    lib.concatMap
      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (lib.hasPrefix "bind") (builtins.attrNames s));
  macKeybindings = pkgs.runCommand "orca-mac-keybindings" {
    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper ];
  } ''
    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \
      > $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json
    # The merge runs Orca's conflict check on the merged file at activation,
    # so the keybinding module (and its one sibling import) ships alongside.
    mkdir -p $out/lib/shared
    cp -r app/out/shared/keybindings.js app/out/shared/keybindings \
      app/out/shared/tui-agent-display-names.js $out/lib/shared/
    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \
      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
  '';
  # ~/.orca/keybindings.json is Orca's read-write state: its settings UI saves
  # into the same platforms.linux section, by atomic rename, so a home.file
  # symlink would be replaced on the first edit. So the generated keys are
  # merged into whatever Orca last wrote, owning only what the last merge
  # wrote (a sidecar records it), and a UI edit outranks them -- the rules
  # are at the top of nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js.
  # tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh.
in
{
  home.packages =
    lib.optionals (!isDarwin && isDesktop) [
    # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
    # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
    # same reason parsec gets it.
      (config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca)
    ];

  home.activation.orcaMacKeybindings = lib.mkIf (!isDarwin && isDesktop)
    (lib.hm.dag.entryAfter [ "writeBoundary" ] ''
      $DRY_RUN_CMD ${macKeybindings}/bin/orca-mac-keybindings
    '');
}

     - Alt+3 selects tab 3 before the change, and does nothing after it.

    - the Mac table and no Mod left (case 1)
    - the Hyprland filter (2, 3)
    - fresh file and idempotency (4)
    - keeping UI edits outside owned keys (5)
    - leaving unparseable or empty files alone (6, 9)
    - dropping stale keys while keeping UI-changed ones, across two runs (7)
    - withdrawing on a clash, restoring the UI's value, and a later UI edit on a withdrawn action (8, 8b, 8c)
    - the IO-failure exit 0 (10)
    - the digit family and untranslatable binds in the generator (11, 12)

    - the tab/workspace shadowing above
    - the bad-sidecar refusal (merge-js lines 79-82): no case writes a malformed sidecar
    - the non-object-JSON refusal (line 58)
    - legacy root-shape `common`, string/null shorthand, and a withdrawn key falling back to the common section (lines 107-113, 132)

  - A running Orca only picks up the merged file after a restart or `keybindings:reload`.
  - Orca's conflict check fills in defaults and normalises chords, so lower-case hand edits are still caught.
  - The withdrawal loop always terminates.
  - All of shiori's Hyprland binds live in `hyprland.nix` settings, so the generator sees every one.

  # Chords Hyprland binds are skipped and those actions keep their Linux Ctrl
  # default -- the compositor would eat them, leaving a dead key. On shiori
  # that is 19 actions, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,
  # plus Super+B/N/E, the digits, and their Shift forms; so Ctrl+F/P/B/N/E stay
  # Orca's. And an action whose Mac chord such a fallback would shadow falls
  # back too: tab.selectByIndex keeps Alt+1..9, since Ctrl+1..9 stays the
  # workspaces'. The build log lists every one.
  #
  # A running Orca reads the file once; after a switch, restart it (or run its
  # keybindings reload) for the new table to apply.

    lib.concatMap
      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      # bind, bindl, binde, ...: the lists. `binds` is a config section, a set.
      (builtins.filter (k: lib.hasPrefix "bind" k && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s));""")

    node -e "require('$out/lib/shared/keybindings.js')"
    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \\
      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
""","""    makeWrapper ${pkgs.nodejs}/bin/node $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings \\
      --add-flags "${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings-merge.js} $out/lib/shared $out/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
    # One real merge, so an Orca bump that moves an import or an export the
    # merge uses fails here, not as a warning at every activation.
    HOME=$TMPDIR/home $out/bin/orca-mac-keybindings 2> merge.err
    if [ -s merge.err ] || [ ! -s $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json ]; then
      cat merge.err >&2; exit 1
    fi
""")

p='tests/orca-mac-keybindings.sh'; s=open(p).read()
rep("""(builtins.filter (k: builtins.substring 0 4 k == "bind") (builtins.attrNames s))""","""(builtins.filter (k: builtins.substring 0 4 k == "bind" && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s))""")

input.old_string: # 8. A UI shortcut on a generated chord
input.new_string:
# 7d. A generated key reset in the UI (absent, though claimed) comes back:
#     the reset target is this table.
H="$T/reset"; mkdir -p "$H/.orca"
echo '{"version":1,"keybindings":{},"platforms":{"darwin":{},"linux":{},"win32":{}}}' > "$H/.orca/keybindings.json"
echo '{"linux":{"tab.close":["Cmd+W"]}}' > "$H/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json"
HOME=$H "$MERGE" >/dev/null 2>&1
got=$(jq -c '.platforms.linux["tab.close"]' "$H/.orca/keybindings.json")
[ "$got" = '["Cmd+W"]' ] && pass "UI reset of a generated key re-applies it" || fail "reset" "got $got"

# 8. A UI shortcut on a generated chord

content.text: <total_tokens>14683685 tokens left</total_tokens>

Round 6 had two Importants, both now fixed, with 27/27 tests passing at `5c41539b`:
1. **Ownership per key (type-design):** a value you set on any action the merge hasn't claimed is now treated as yours. That covers a first merge into an existing file and actions that only become generated later.
2. **Build breakage (error-handling):** an ordinary Hyprland bind like a bare `Print` key or `SUPER + grave` no longer breaks the build. Only an unknown modifier fails it; keys Orca can't name are skipped with a log line, and Hyprland's aliases are mapped.

Also cleaned up: the merge's restore path, which per-key ownership made unreachable, is gone. The build-time merge check now confirms the table actually landed. Two more tests pin a UI reset re-applying the generated key, and a valid shared binding still counting when the Linux-specific entry for that action is invalid.

Round 6's correctness review is the only one still out. Once it's read, round 7 starts on the new HEAD. Two clean rounds in a row on one HEAD, and then I merge to master and run `hms`.

Round 7 ended with three reviewers clean and error-handling reporting one Important. It's fixed, tests pass 29/29, and it's committed as `b1909c92`.

The problem was the rule for Hyprland binds the generator can't parse: it assumed any such key could never be an Orca chord. Some are Orca chords under another spelling, for example `KP_Add` (Orca's NumpadAdd, zoom in) and lowercase `prior` (PageUp). Those would have shipped as dead keys.

3. **Smaller fixes:** a new test checks that a bare `Delete` bind counts as taken, and the test script now shows the real nix error instead of a misleading "not on this host".
4. **Deferred, two nits, both recorded:** an edge where a UI value exactly equals the generated one, and a millisecond race with a running Orca's own save.

Round 8 (all four angles) is running on `b1909c92`. Correctness is also checking that utsuho's Hyprland binds still build.

Round 8 found one more Important, now fixed. Tests pass 31/31, and it's committed as `78ed7b94`. Round 9 (all four angles) is running.

**The bug:** Hyprland matches a bind like `SUPER + SHIFT + equal` on the unshifted key, but Orca sees that press as `Cmd+Shift+Plus`. The generator didn't count it as taken, so it shipped a dead zoom-in chord. Checked against Orca's own key matcher, only two keys behave this way: `equal`→`Plus` and `minus`→`Underscore`. Both spellings now count as taken. Your current `SUPER + SHIFT + semicolon` bind was already handled correctly.

**Also fixed:**
- `META` is now treated as an alias for Super.
- Media keys are skipped whatever their capitalisation.
- Keycode binds such as `code:41` now fail the build with their own message.

**Where this stands:** 9 rounds, with roughly one new Important per round. Each one has been real but increasingly edge-case: Hyprland bind forms you don't use today. The remaining cost of each round is a few minutes and four agents.

**Decision for you:** keep looping until two consecutive rounds are clean, or ship once round 9 has no Critical/Important findings. Shipping means merging to master and running `hms`, ~10–15 min. Either way, the Super+F/P/N/B question from earlier still stands.

       || ! grep -q '"Cmd+W"' $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json \
       || ! grep -q '"Alt+0, Alt+Shift+0"' $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.json \
       || [ ! -s $TMPDIR/home/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json ]; then

Round 10 correctness raised a genuine design trade-off rather than a bug, so it's your call.

**The problem:** Orca's settings UI saves "set this back to the Linux default" (for example, `tab.close` → Ctrl+W) as a key deletion, which is identical to "Reset". The merge reads an absent claimed key as a reset and writes the Mac chord back. So if you pick a Linux default in the UI, it silently reverts on the next `hms`. Orca's file gives no way to tell the two actions apart.

questions.question: When you delete or reset a generated shortcut in Orca's UI, what should the next `hms` do?

options.label: Respect it (Recommended)
options.description: An absent key the merge once wrote stays absent, so the action keeps Orca's Linux default. The UI always wins. To get a Mac chord back after resetting it, delete its line from ~/.orca/keybindings.nix-owned.json.

options.label: Re-apply Mac chord
options.description: Current behaviour: an absent key comes back as the Mac chord at the next switch. Picking the Linux default in the UI doesn't stick. Documented as a limitation.

OWNED="$PKG/share/orca-mac-keybindings.json"
[ -x "$MERGE" ] && [ -f "$OWNED" ] || { echo "$PKG lacks bin/ or share/" >&2; exit 1; }

T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
jqo() { jq -c "$1" "$OWNED"; }

# 1. The Mac table, on Super: clipboard and tabs are the reason this exists.
for c in 'terminal.copySelection:["Cmd+C"]' 'terminal.paste:["Cmd+V"]' \
         'tab.close:["Cmd+W"]' 'tab.newTerminal:["Cmd+T"]'; do
  id=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
  got=$(jqo ".[\"$id\"]")
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$id = $want" || fail "$id" "got $got, want $want"
done
got=$(jqo '[.[][] | select(test("(^|\\+)Mod\\+"))]')
[ "$got" = "[]" ] && pass "no Mod (= Ctrl on Linux) left" || fail "Mod" "still bound: $got"

# 2. Nothing the generator emits is a Hyprland chord.
nix eval --json "$HM.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings" --apply \
  's: builtins.concatMap (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      (builtins.filter (k: builtins.substring 0 4 k == "bind" && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s))' \
  > "$T/hypr.json" || { echo "could not evaluate Hyprland binds (above)" >&2; exit 1; }
# Hyprland "SUPER + SHIFT + W" -> Orca "Cmd+Shift+W"; letters upper-cased, the
# keys Orca spells differently renamed. Mouse and switch binds never match.
jq -r '.[] | split(" + ") | map(
    {SUPER:"Cmd",CTRL:"Ctrl",ALT:"Alt",SHIFT:"Shift",
     return:"Enter",left:"ArrowLeft",right:"ArrowRight",up:"ArrowUp",down:"ArrowDown",
     space:"Space",semicolon:"Semicolon"}[.] // (if length == 1 then ascii_upcase else . end))
  | join("+")' "$T/hypr.json" | sort -u > "$T/hypr.txt"
grep -qx 'Cmd+F' "$T/hypr.txt" || { echo "Hyprland bind list lacks Super+F; harness is broken" >&2; exit 1; }
jq -r '.[][]' "$OWNED" | sort -u > "$T/owned.txt"
clash=$(comm -12 "$T/hypr.txt" "$T/owned.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')
[ -z "$clash" ] && pass "no override is a Hyprland chord" || fail "hyprland" "both bind: $clash"

# 3. A chord Hyprland owns leaves its action on Orca's Linux default, not unbound.
got=$(jqo 'has("editor.find"), has("worktree.quickOpen")' | tr '\n' ' ')
[ "$got" = "false false " ] && pass "Super+F/Super+P actions keep their Linux defaults" \
  || fail "fallback" "editor.find/worktree.quickOpen overridden: $got"

# 4. Fresh box: the file is created in the shape Orca writes.
H="$T/fresh"; mkdir -p "$H"

# Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. Ctrl+C is
  # SIGINT again, not copy; Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+PageUp/Down cycle tabs, as on a
  # Mac.
  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
  # Chords Hyprland binds are skipped and those actions keep their Linux Ctrl
  # default -- the compositor would eat them, leaving a dead key. On shiori
  # that is 19 actions, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,
  # plus Super+B/N/E, the digits, and their Shift forms; so Ctrl+F/P/B/N/E stay
  # Orca's. And an action whose Mac chord such a fallback would shadow falls
  # back too: tab.selectByIndex keeps Alt+1..9, since Ctrl+1..9 stays the
  # workspaces'. The build log lists every one.
  #
  # A running Orca reads the file once; after a switch, restart it (or run its
  # keybindings reload) for the new table to apply.
  hyprlandChords = let s = config.wayland.windowManager.hyprland.settings; in
    lib.concatMap
      (k: map (b: if builtins.isAttrs b && b ? _args then builtins.head b._args else b) s.${k})
      # bind, bindl, binde, ...: the lists. `binds` is a config section, a set.
      (builtins.filter (k: lib.hasPrefix "bind" k && builtins.isList s.${k}) (builtins.attrNames s));
  macKeybindings = pkgs.runCommand "orca-mac-keybindings" {
    nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgs.nodejs pkgs.asar pkgs.makeWrapper pkgs.jq ];
  } ''
    asar extract ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar app
    mkdir -p $out/share $out/bin
    node ${./nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js} app/out/shared \
      ${pkgs.writeText "hyprland-chords.json" (builtins.toJSON hyprlandChords)} \

input.content:
---
name: mac-binds-leave-ctrl-to-terminal
description: "Mac-like keybinds" here means Super-as-Cmd so Ctrl/Meta stay free for emacs keys in the terminal; never leave app actions on Ctrl/Alt defaults.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When configuring an app with "my mac-like keybinds", the goal is not just Super-for-Cmd: it is that **Ctrl and Alt (Meta) chords stay the terminal's**, so emacs/readline keys reach the shell. An action whose Super chord Hyprland owns must be **unbound**, not left on the app's Linux Ctrl default; the app's own Ctrl/Alt chords (even ones its Mac table uses) go too. Exceptions are explicit pins (Orca: find on Ctrl+S, i.e. emacs isearch) and chords a terminal cannot send (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PageUp/Down).

**Why:** user, 2026-10-24, on Orca falling back to Ctrl+F/Ctrl+P: "find should be C-s and just get rid of go to file. the whole point is to not steal emacs binds from the terminal, this is horrible."

**How to apply:** for any new app keymap (Orca, Zed, editors, Electron apps), audit the *effective* table for Ctrl-/Alt-only chords before shipping, and ask about the few worth pinning rather than defaulting to the app's Ctrl binds. Existing schemes: gtk mac-bindings and ghostty super+c/v in home.nix, orca.nix's orcaPinned.

---
name: mac-binds-leave-ctrl-to-terminal
description: "Mac-like keybinds" here means Super-as-Cmd so Ctrl/Meta stay free for emacs keys in the terminal; never leave app actions on Ctrl/Alt defaults.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When configuring an app with "my mac-like keybinds", the goal is not just Super-for-Cmd: it is that **Ctrl and Alt (Meta) chords stay the terminal's**, so emacs/readline keys reach the shell. An action whose Super chord Hyprland owns must be **unbound**, not left on the app's Linux Ctrl default; the app's own Ctrl/Alt chords (even ones its Mac table uses) go too. Exceptions are explicit pins (Orca: find on Ctrl+S, i.e. emacs isearch) and chords a terminal cannot send (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PageUp/Down).

**Why:** user, 2026-10-24, on Orca falling back to Ctrl+F/Ctrl+P: "find should be C-s and just get rid of go to file. the whole point is to not steal emacs binds from the terminal, this is horrible."

**How to apply:** for any new app keymap (Orca, Zed, editors, Electron apps), audit the *effective* table for Ctrl-/Alt-only chords before shipping, and ask about the few worth pinning rather than defaulting to the app's Ctrl binds. Existing schemes: gtk mac-bindings and ghostty super+c/v in home.nix, orca.nix's orcaPinned.

content.text:
I've changed the keymap so Orca no longer takes Ctrl or Alt keys from the terminal. It's committed on the branch as `0b435f2e`, all 31 tests pass, and the final review round you asked for is running now.

What the keymap now does:
1. **Super does what Cmd does on a Mac:**
   - Super+C / Super+V copy and paste in Orca's terminal.
   - Super+T opens a tab, Super+W closes it.
   - Super+S saves, Super+J switches worktree.
   - Super+= / Super+− zoom.
2. **No Ctrl- or Alt-only shortcuts are left.** Ctrl+C is SIGINT again, and C-a, C-e, M-f and the rest reach emacs and readline. The only exceptions:
   - Find is Ctrl+S in the editor, browser, chat and settings.
   - Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+PageUp/Down still cycle tabs; a terminal can't receive those anyway.
3. **17 actions are now unbound:**
   - Go to file and terminal search.
   - Tab-by-number and workspace-by-number.
   - The sidebar toggles, new worktree, voice dictation, zoom reset, new browser tab, open markdown, word wrap, and terminal split-down.

   Most of these had Mac chords that Hyprland already uses, and their only other option was a Ctrl key.
4. **I took one call you didn't make: terminal search is unbound rather than Ctrl+S**, so C-s stays the shell's own search. Putting it on Ctrl+S is one line in `orcaPinned` in `orca.nix`.
5. **Resetting a shortcut in Orca's settings brings the Mac chord back at the next `hms`**, as you chose. To keep an action unbound, unbind it or set a different key instead of resetting. This is noted in `orca.nix`.

I saved a memory that "mac-like keybinds" means leaving Ctrl and Meta to the terminal, so future app keymaps start from that.

Once the review is in, I'll fix anything blocking, merge to master and run `hms` (~10–15 min). Then restart Orca, since it only reads the keybinding file at startup.

content.text: <total_tokens>14546142 tokens left</total_tokens>

Round 11 found one Important, now fixed and committed as `d65cb945` (31/31 tests pass).

**The bug:** when a generated shortcut clashed with one you'd set in Orca's UI, the merge withdrew the generated one by deleting it. Deleting it put the action back on Orca's Ctrl default: Ctrl+T for new tab, Ctrl+W for close tab. That is exactly what your Ctrl-is-the-terminal's rule forbids.

**The fix:** a withdrawn shortcut is now unbound instead of deleted. A shortcut you set on that action later is still treated as yours.

I also cleaned up some code in the generator that could no longer run. If `orcaPinned` is given a single chord instead of a list, the error now names the action.

Round 11 status:
- Security and error-handling came back clean.
- Type-design found the Important above.
- Correctness, the last of the four, is still running.

Once correctness is in and anything Critical or Important is fixed:
1. Check whether master has moved, then merge `orca-mac-keys` into it.
2. Run `hms` (~10–15 min of CI).
3. Restart Orca so it rereads the keybinding file.

Orca is now set up with your Mac-style keybinds, and `hms` applied them (exit 0). They take effect once you restart Orca, since it only reads the keybinding file at startup.

I checked the live `~/.orca/keybindings.json`:
- **Super does Cmd's job:** Super+C / Super+V copy and paste in Orca's terminal, Super+T opens a tab and Super+W closes it.
- **Find is Ctrl+S** in the editor, browser, chat and settings.
- **Unbound:** terminal search, so C-s stays the shell's, and go to file.
- **No other Ctrl or Alt chords:** the only Ctrl/Alt bindings in the file are those four Ctrl+S finds, so emacs keys reach the shell. Orca's Ctrl+Tab default also stays, since Orca's terminal receives it as a plain Tab.

Two things that behave differently from what you might expect:
- **Actions that lost their chords:** where Hyprland already uses the Mac chord, the action is now unbound rather than falling back to Ctrl. That covers sidebar toggles, new worktree, workspace-by-number and voice dictation, among others. Tab-by-number, word wrap and next/previous terminal tab are unbound too, because the Mac table's own Ctrl/Alt chords for them were dropped. To give any of them a key, add it to `orcaPinned` in `orca.nix`.
- **Reset in Orca's settings:** resetting a shortcut there brings the Mac chord back at the next `hms`. To keep a key off, unbind it or set another key instead.

I deferred the remaining minor review items; none affects today's config. The `orca-mac-keys` worktree is still in `.drovr/wt/`, and I can remove it if you like.

- Super+C / Super+V should copy and paste.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/worktrees

# Worktrees

## Why

A drovr run edits `project_dir` across every phase. By default that is the
invoking checkout, so a run in flight blocks you from touching the repo and
leaves uncommitted changes strewn across it. A **git worktree** gives the run its
own checkout on its own branch, sharing the object store — the invoking checkout
stays clean and usable *for other work*. This is the physical form of the
single-writer rule: **one run, one worktree, one writer.**

That does **not** mean the driver stays behind in the invoking checkout. The
worktree is where the run happens, and the driver goes there too — see "The
flow" below.

## When to isolate

Reach for `--worktree` when:

- You want the main checkout left free for other work while the run proceeds.
  (Free for *other* work — the driver of the run itself moves into the worktree.)
- The run is large or long enough that half-finished, uncommitted state in your
  real tree would be a hazard.
- Multiple runs may touch the same repo — each gets its own branch, no collisions.

Skip it for a quick inline change you will finish and commit yourself, or in a
non-git directory (it is a hard error there — isolation needs a repo).

## The flow

```
drovr new <run> --worktree        # .drovr/wt/<run> on branch drovr/<run>; project_dir points there
EnterWorktree({path: ".drovr/wt/<run>"})   # ← YOU move too. Do this NEXT, before anything else.
  ...phases run isolated in the worktree, never the outer checkout...
drovr cleanup <run>               # commits the run's work, prunes the worktree, KEEPS the branch
```

- Set a standing default with `worktree = true` in config; `--no-worktree`
  overrides per-run.
- `.drovr/wt/` is ignored via `.git/info/exclude` — the tracked `.gitignore` is
  never touched.

### ⚠️ The `EnterWorktree` line is not optional — drovr cannot move you

`drovr new --worktree` **prints** the worktree path; it does not put you in it.
Nothing in drovr ever changes your directory, and nothing can: a subprocess
cannot change its parent's working directory. Moving is your job, and it is the
step drivers skip.

Skip it and you are still in the invoking checkout, so every bare `git status`,
`git log` and `git diff` you run answers about **main, not your run's branch** —
including other agents' uncommitted files, which you will read as your own. On a
repo with several runs in flight that is how one agent clobbers another.

`cd` will not do it: the Bash tool's cwd resets to the session's primary
directory after every call. Use the harness tool:

```
EnterWorktree({path: ".drovr/wt/<run>"})   # switches the SESSION's dir; persists
ExitWorktree({action: ...})                # when the run is done
```

Then stay there. Do not operate from the main checkout for the rest of the run.

## Handing the branch back — drovr never merges

Cleanup leaves you a reviewable branch `drovr/<run>` and prints the merge command.
**You** drive the merge — drovr does not act on your shared branch. Review it like
any other branch, then `git merge drovr/<run>` (or open a PR).

`ExitWorktree` **first**, then `drovr cleanup`, then merge — in that order. The
merge belongs in the checkout you are merging *into*, and cleanup prunes the
worktree out from under you if you are still standing in it.

`drovr cleanup <run> --purge` force-removes the worktree, deletes the branch, and
drops the run dir — use it to discard a run whose work you don't want.

## Bind checklists to tracked task state

Isolating a run and handing its branch back are both multi-step flows.

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

## Discipline

- **Enter the worktree, and work only from there.** See "The `EnterWorktree`
  line is not optional" above. A driver still sitting in the invoking checkout
  is reading the wrong tree, silently, for the whole run.
- **One writer per worktree.** Fan-out investigation still goes to read-only
  explorers, never parallel writers — the worktree isolates the run from *other
  checkouts*, not the single-writer rule from itself.
- **The worktree belongs to the run's PHASE AGENTS. The driver drives and reads.**
  Do not hand-edit files there while a phase is live — not docs, not a `git
  merge`, not "just one fix". The phase agent is that worktree's writer, and a
  review panel may be reading those exact files: a merge started under a running
  panel puts conflict markers in front of the reviewers, and they will review
  them. If the driver must change something, wait for the phase to finish, or
  send the work to the phase agent.
- **Uncommitted work is safe:** cleanup commits before pruning, and git refuses to
  remove a dirty worktree without `--purge` — it will never silently discard work.

Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/worktrees

# Worktrees

## Why

A drovr run edits `project_dir` across every phase. By default that is the
invoking checkout, so a run in flight blocks you from touching the repo and
leaves uncommitted changes strewn across it. A **git worktree** gives the run its
own checkout on its own branch, sharing the object store — the invoking checkout
stays clean and usable *for other work*. This is the physical form of the
single-writer rule: **one run, one worktree, one writer.**

That does **not** mean the driver stays behind in the invoking checkout. The
worktree is where the run happens, and the driver goes there too — see "The
flow" below.

## When to isolate

Reach for `--worktree` when:

- You want the main checkout left free for other work while the run proceeds.
  (Free for *other* work — the driver of the run itself moves into the worktree.)
- The run is large or long enough that half-finished, uncommitted state in your
  real tree would be a hazard.
- Multiple runs may touch the same repo — each gets its own branch, no collisions.

Skip it for a quick inline change you will finish and commit yourself, or in a
non-git directory (it is a hard error there — isolation needs a repo).

## The flow

```
drovr new <run> --worktree        # .drovr/wt/<run> on branch drovr/<run>; project_dir points there
EnterWorktree({path: ".drovr/wt/<run>"})   # ← YOU move too. Do this NEXT, before anything else.
  ...phases run isolated in the worktree, never the outer checkout...
drovr cleanup <run>               # commits the run's work, prunes the worktree, KEEPS the branch
```

- Set a standing default with `worktree = true` in config; `--no-worktree`
  overrides per-run.
- `.drovr/wt/` is ignored via `.git/info/exclude` — the tracked `.gitignore` is
  never touched.

### ⚠️ The `EnterWorktree` line is not optional — drovr cannot move you

`drovr new --worktree` **prints** the worktree path; it does not put you in it.
Nothing in drovr ever changes your directory, and nothing can: a subprocess
cannot change its parent's working directory. Moving is your job, and it is the
step drivers skip.

Skip it and you are still in the invoking checkout, so every bare `git status`,
`git log` and `git diff` you run answers about **main, not your run's branch** —
including other agents' uncommitted files, which you will read as your own. On a
repo with several runs in flight that is how one agent clobbers another.

`cd` will not do it: the Bash tool's cwd resets to the session's primary
directory after every call. Use the harness tool:

```
EnterWorktree({path: ".drovr/wt/<run>"})   # switches the SESSION's dir; persists
ExitWorktree({action: ...})                # when the run is done
```

Then stay there. Do not operate from the main checkout for the rest of the run.

## Handing the branch back — drovr never merges

Cleanup leaves you a reviewable branch `drovr/<run>` and prints the merge command.
**You** drive the merge — drovr does not act on your shared branch. Review it like
any other branch, then `git merge drovr/<run>` (or open a PR).

`ExitWorktree` **first**, then `drovr cleanup`, then merge — in that order. The
merge belongs in the checkout you are merging *into*, and cleanup prunes the
worktree out from under you if you are still standing in it.

`drovr cleanup <run> --purge` force-removes the worktree, deletes the branch, and
drops the run dir — use it to discard a run whose work you don't want.

## Bind checklists to tracked task state

Isolating a run and handing its branch back are both multi-step flows.

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

## Discipline

- **Enter the worktree, and work only from there.** See "The `EnterWorktree`
  line is not optional" above. A driver still sitting in the invoking checkout
  is reading the wrong tree, silently, for the whole run.
- **One writer per worktree.** Fan-out investigation still goes to read-only
  explorers, never parallel writers — the worktree isolates the run from *other
  checkouts*, not the single-writer rule from itself.
- **The worktree belongs to the run's PHASE AGENTS. The driver drives and reads.**
  Do not hand-edit files there while a phase is live — not docs, not a `git
  merge`, not "just one fix". The phase agent is that worktree's writer, and a
  review panel may be reading those exact files: a merge started under a running
  panel puts conflict markers in front of the reviewers, and they will review
  them. If the driver must change something, wait for the phase to finish, or
  send the work to the phase agent.
- **Uncommitted work is safe:** cleanup commits before pruning, and git refuses to
  remove a dirty worktree without `--purge` — it will never silently discard work.
